questions.question: Define a source document and give four reasons why businesses must keep source documents.
questions.expected_answer: A source document is the original, first written (or electronic) evidence of a transaction, containing the details needed to record it: date, parties, description, amount and document number. Reasons: it is the basis for recording in the journals; it is proof in disputes; it supports internal control (pre-numbered documents show missing records and possible theft); it is required by law — records must be kept for five years for SARS, and a valid tax invoice is needed to claim input VAT; auditors, banks and investors use it to check the accuracy of the financial statements.

questions.question: Describe each of the following and state whether it is recorded in the CRJ or the CPJ of a service business: duplicate receipt, cash register roll, deposit slip, EFT payment confirmation, bank statement, original cash invoice from a supplier.
questions.expected_answer: Duplicate receipt: copy kept by the business of a receipt issued for money received — CRJ. Cash register roll: record of all till sales with the daily total — CRJ. Deposit slip: proof of cash deposited at the bank, used to check the daily bank total in the CRJ. EFT payment confirmation: proof of an electronic payment made — CPJ. Bank statement: monthly list of all transactions from the bank — CRJ for direct deposits, EFTs received and interest earned; CPJ for bank charges, debit orders and card payments. Original cash invoice from a supplier: bill for goods or services paid for immediately — CPJ.

questions.question: A plumber charges R800 labour and R200 parts, excluding VAT, and is paid immediately. Calculate the VAT and invoice total at 15%. Which copy of the invoice does each party keep, and in which journal does each record it?
questions.expected_answer: Subtotal = 800 + 200 = R1 000. VAT = 15% × 1 000 = R150. Total = R1 150. The plumber (seller) keeps the duplicate and records it in the CRJ as money received. The homeowner (buyer) keeps the original; if she were a business she would record it in the CPJ as money paid.
